_note: buck-5v3a MERGED constraint set (P2). Net names are CANONICAL - the schematic must produce exactly these (architecture/sheets.md s3). Refdes are BINDING (sheets.md s2). Derivations: power_tree.md (loss model, widths), stackup.md (thermal, layer count). Copy to kicad/constraints.json at P5 and keep ONE copy - two copies gave two different answers on a prior board (LEARNINGS 2026-07-29).
_superseded: research/power.json's power_constraints/thermal_constraints are superseded by this file: /VIN -> /VIN_RAW, /VIN_F -> /VIN_FUSED, /SW and +5V ceilings 3.5 -> 3.6 A (peak I_L re-derived at 450 kHz with L = 6.8 uH), U1 power_w 0.8 -> 0.95 W (real 74/40 mohm RDS(on), DS41948 p.5, not the assumed 45/20 mohm class).

power._why: J1.1 -> F1. Operating worst case is 2.35 A at the 7 V corner; 3.0 A is the design ceiling so the copper also survives the 4 A fuse's non-blow current. pdn false: nothing decouples a pre-protection stub by design.
F1 -> Q1 source. Same budget as /VIN_RAW.

Protected rail: Q1 drain, D2, C1-C3, U1 VIN, EN divider. RMS in the Cin->VIN->GND loop is Io*sqrt(D) = 2.54 A at the 7 V corner, covered by the 3.0 A ceiling. MUST BE VIA-FREE: at 0.5 A/via one via demands 6 in that cluster (net-wide rule, LEARNINGS 2026-07-28).
Peak inductor current 3.59 A at the 18 V corner. dT 20 not 10 deliberately: /SW is the aggressor node and must stay SMALL (buck.md s5) - 0.78 mm at 2 oz instead of 1.16 mm. ZERO VIAS, F.Cu only.

L1 -> C5/C6 -> J2 carries the full peak inductor current. 1.16 mm at 2 oz. ZERO VIAS - a via-free pour is also exempt from check_current's pour-neck test. P6/P7 must add an override for the D1 LED tap (~0.05 A, ~6 mm radius) once positions exist, else every 0.25 mm branch reads as an undersized 3.6 A track.

Declared explicitly rather than left to check_current's derived-return synthesis (which downgrades everything to advisory): on a 15 W converter the return deserves ERROR-class pour-neck checking at the full budget. plane_fed makes the unsatisfiable per-cluster via count advisory (LEARNINGS 2026-07-29).

thermal._power_basis: 0.881 W modelled at the 7 V low-line corner for AP63356QZV-7 with RDS(on) 92/48 mohm at ~105 C (DS41948 p.5 typ 74/40 at 25 C, scaled by Fig.5), + ~8 % for the unpublished tr/tf and for part-to-part RDS(on) spread - the datasheet publishes NO maximum RDS(on), which is itself the risk this margin covers. Re-derive if P3 substitutes a different regulator. Sensitivity: at 1.3x typ RDS(on) P_IC is ~1.10 W -> 56.2 C rise -> T_j ~106 C, which still clears the part's 150 C recommended max by 44 C but trips this gate. That is the intended behaviour.
thermal._dt_basis: REWRITTEN 2026-08-09 (P2 revisit, reports/thermal-recheck.md). 55 C allowed rise = the SOFT 105 C junction target (requirements s3) at 50 C ambient (A9). H1-d ruled that 105 C is a soft design target, NOT a filter: the BINDING limit is the part's own TJ 150 C recommended operating max (= dt_c 100) and 170 C absolute (= dt_c 120). 55 is kept because it is the design target, it is met with margin, and it is the only machine-visible thermal discipline on this board. Machine-verified with check_thermal on a probe carrying U1's REAL 9-land pattern with NO exposed pad: 48.55 C rise on 4 layers (PASS, 6.45 C margin, T_j 98.6 C at 0.95 W / 95.0 C at the modelled 0.881 W) vs 70.15 C on 2 layers (FAIL). WITHDRAWN: the previous claim that this entry encodes the stackup decision - a 2-layer build does fail the gate, but the real 4L-vs-2L junction-temperature gap on a 2 oz-outer board is ~3 C, not ~20 C. ALSO WITHDRAWN: the previous note that the other 0.37-0.60 W of board loss 'adds ~10 C that this number does not contain'. A first-principles model run WITH that loss injected gives an effective 44-58 C/W, which brackets the gate's 51.1 C/W - the +10 C allowance in stackup.md s2.4 was double counting. T_j at the 7 V corner is ~95 C, not ~105 C.
thermal._vias_basis: REWRITTEN 2026-08-09 - U1 HAS NO EXPOSED PAD (reports/u1-land-ruling.md). The heat exits are the GND land (pad 8) and the VIN land (pad 1), each 1.500 x 0.750 mm, per DS41948 p.25 layout rules 7-8 and Figure 47. GND side: 12 vias of 0.55 mm pad / 0.30 mm drill, through F.Cu->B.Cu so each picks up In1, In2 and B.Cu, placed as a ~1.0 mm-pitch field in the top GND pour AROUND the GND land - >= 8 with centres within 2.0 mm of the land edge, all 12 within 4.0 mm of the U1 centroid. Never below 0.85 mm pitch (0.55 mm pads at the 0.1016 mm clearance of 4layer_2oz need 0.65 mm centre-to-centre and the pour must stay connected between them). NOT the 0.45/0.20 rule-class minimum: a 0.30 mm barrel at 25 um plating is 50.9 C/W to In1 against 79.9 C/W for a 0.20 mm barrel. NO via-in-pad on the GND land: two in-pad vias are worth ~0.2 C/W and would put open 0.30 mm holes in the part's only thermal and mechanical joint - allowed only if JLC POFV resin-plug-and-cap is ordered at P10, and not recommended. VIN side gets ZERO vias (this board has no VIN plane, because rule 6 puts GND on In1 and In2, and +VIN must stay via-free for check_current's net-wide via rule); its substitute is >= 60 mm2 of contiguous F.Cu +VIN pour joined to the VIN land over unbroken In1 GND. SUPERSEDED: 'a 3x3 array of 0.3 mm vias at 1.0 mm pitch inside the exposed-pad land plus >= 3 in the surrounding top-side GND pour'. ENFORCEMENT: check_thermal does not raise its via warning at this power/dt (need_vias false: dt/power = 57.9 > the 51.1 C/W floor), and it was machine-verified to return the IDENTICAL 51.1 C/W / 48.55 C result on a probe stripped of every thermal via AND the entire top GND pour. This floor, the 200 mm2 F.Cu GND pour and the 60 mm2 +VIN pour are enforced by P6/P7 review only.

planes._why: Solid GND, unbroken under U1 and the whole Cin/VIN/GND hot loop - no signal, no +5V and no split within 6 mm of the U1 centroid. Return plane AND primary heat spreader, 0.4284 mm below F.Cu. CORRECTED 2026-08-09: it sits below the GND-land via field and below the +VIN pour, NOT below an 'exposed-pad via array' - the part has no exposed pad. On this board the In1 return plane is the REASON for 4 layers; its thermal contribution is real but small (the 0.5 oz inners are 18 % of the board's copper).

GND again, NOT the +5V rail. Overrides planes_gen's 4-layer default (In2 = dominant power net): +5V travels ~20 mm on F.Cu and needs no plane, while a second GND plane is worth more as thermal mass and lets the GND-land via field land on copper at both inner layers. DS41948 PCB Layout rule 6 asks for exactly this ('use at least the 2nd and 3rd layers as GND'). CORRECTED 2026-08-09: 'lets the EP via array see copper on both inner layers' - there is no EP via array; the vias are in the pour around the GND land. Note this choice is why rule 8 ('vias ... under the VIN plane') cannot be honoured literally: there is no VIN plane, so the VIN land is served by F.Cu pour area instead.
Bottom heat-radiating surface and via-array landing. Kept clear of SMT parts (A11).

Top GND pour joined to U1's GND LAND (pad 8) - >= 200 mm2 contiguous, carrying the 12-via field of thermal[0]._vias_basis, and the hot loop's return. Poured at P7.2 after routing. CORRECTED 2026-08-09: 'joined to U1's exposed-pad land' - there is no exposed pad; F.Cu is the layer the die actually touches, through the GND, VIN and SW lands. A matching contiguous +VIN pour of >= 60 mm2 must be joined to the VIN land (pad 1) on the same layer - that is the VIN-side heat exit and it is NOT a GND pour, so planes_gen will not create it; P7 must pour it explicitly.

keepouts.reason: A11: JLCPCB top-side SMT assembly only - the bottom side stays clear as a thermal/return plane. J1/J2 are THT and unaffected.

placement._separation_note: min_mm is CENTROID-to-centroid and is a place_anneal cost term, not a legality rule. 8 mm between a 3x2 mm U1 and an 8x8 mm L1 is a ~2.5 mm body gap - a deliberate compromise: DS41948 rule 3 ('inductor as close to SW as possible') and buck.md s5 switch-node containment WIN over research/power.md's '>= 5 mm from U1' thermal preference, because a long /SW polygon is a worse problem than two adjacent 0.9 W and 0.3 W bodies on a board with two solid GND planes. 15 mm U1<->F1 keeps the fuse in the cool corner by J1 where its 30 % high-temperature derating does not bite.
placement._edges_note: P6 must set J1/J2 rotation so wire entry faces off-board, and must read it from the 3D model or an orthographic side render - NOT from the silk outline (LEARNINGS 2026-07-28).

_no_high_speed: Deliberately absent. There is no controlled-impedance, standards-bound or clocked net on this board. The only fast node is /SW, which is contained on F.Cu over an unbroken In1 GND plane and is governed by the layout rules in blocks.md/stackup.md, not by a return-path check - declaring it would add a check that passes trivially while risking spurious corridor findings.
_no_voltage_pairs: Deliberately absent. Maximum node voltage is 18 V and the maximum pair difference is 18 V, both below check_creepage's 30 V threshold; there is no bridge/AC tap on this board. The voltages list above is declared anyway so that A1's closure of the >30 V flag is machine-visible.
